title: Merge format detectors and introduce lazy shard mapper to cut model load latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Reduce cold-start model load time and simplify code paths by centralizing artifact format detection into the artifact-resolver and replacing eager shard-to-weight mapping with a lazy shard mapper that binds shards on first access. This ticket focuses on the loader side (manifest parsing, format detectors, shard map generation) and the tokenizer handoff contract changes required to avoid redundant passes. Goals: (1) shave median model init time by 25-40% for sharded checkpoints, (2) reduce memory duplication during model bootstrap, (3) simplify the artifact-resolver API so downstream loader stages no longer need ad-hoc format guessing. Scope: manifest/metadata parsers, format-detection module, shard mapping logic, unit tests, integration smoke tests, and small console metric to track init latency. Out of scope: runtime operator scheduling changes and serving-time KV cache behavior (handled in a follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Median cold-start model load latency reduced by >=25% for typical sharded checkpoints (measured on m60-like test cluster)
Artifact resolver exposes a single format API (format:detected) and loader no longer runs its own detection heuristics
Shard map generation moved to lazy mapper with deterministic binding order; no behavioral changes for existing consumers except delayed IO
All existing model ingestion tests pass; add coverage for interleaved tokenizer metadata that previously caused two-pass parsing
Integration smoke test that boots a large 26B sharded model and runs a 64-token generation within SLO
steps: Audit current format detection logic in model-loader and artifact-resolver (week 1)
Prototype lazy shard mapper that returns a proxy mapping and binds concrete shard objects on first read (week 2)
Update tokenizer handoff contract to accept resolver-provided tokenizer metadata and remove duplicate parsing (week 2)
Add unit tests for format detection and lazy binding semantics (week 3)
Run integration benchmarks on staging cluster and iterate on IO concurrency limits (week 3)
Ship change behind runtime feature flag; monitor console metric (model.init.latency) and roll out (week 4)
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after retro discussion on model bootstrap slowness. Put together initial perf numbers from staging: median init 18.2s for 26B sharded model, p95 34s. Current heuristics re-run format sniffing for each checkpoint file which is wasteful.

2026-03-11 - Mateo Ruiz: Built prototype of lazy shard mapper. Key idea: mapper returns lightweight descriptors and performs actual blob fetch/deserialize on first get(). Prototype reduced median init to 12.1s with parallel IO concurrency set to 8.

2026-03-12 - Ling Chen (reviewer): Noted tokenizer metadata can be present in both manifest and per-shard headers; we should define precedence rules in resolver to avoid two-pass tokenization. Suggest adding a resolver field tokenizer_source {manifest|shard|combined}.

2026-03-12 - Mateo Ruiz: Updated design doc to include tokenizer_source and added deterministic binding algorithm (manifest order then shard index). Pushed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7324

2026-03-12 - Security: flagged that lazy binding changes do not alter cryptographic verification but asked to add an HMAC check on first shard fetch. Marking security_review_required=true for follow-up QA.
2026-03-12 - QA: will schedule integration runs on 2026-03-16; need synthetic workload that exercises partial-shard reads.
